---
name: try-omarchy-linux
description: >-
  Use to install, launch, or safely operate the Try Omarchy Flatpak VM (Omarchy
  desktop in a window) on a Linux computer, including one with no working KVM.
---
# Try Omarchy on Linux

Try Omarchy runs the Omarchy desktop (Arch + Hyprland) as a QEMU VM inside a Flatpak app. Official page: https://tryomarchy.com/linux/

## Install
1. Make sure Flatpak is installed and Flathub is added (the runtime comes from Flathub):
   `flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo`
2. Download the app ref and install it per user:
   `curl -LO https://tryomarchy.com/linux.flatpakref`
   `flatpak install --user -y ./linux.flatpakref`
   This adds the `try-omarchy` remote (https://flatpak.tryomarchy.com/repo/) and installs `com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy` plus the GNOME runtime.
3. Verify: `flatpak info --user com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy`

## Decide KVM vs software emulation
- On a normal Linux PC with working `/dev/kvm`, just run `flatpak run com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy`.
- On a cloud VM or bot computer (nested virtualisation), KVM may be missing or may crash the host kernel. Unless the owner has confirmed KVM is safe, use software emulation (TCG) via the wrapper below. Never test KVM by just trying it on a shared machine.

## Software-emulation wrapper
Save as `~/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data/qemu-tcg-wrapper.sh` (inside the app's data dir so the sandbox can see it) and `chmod +x` it:
```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Rewrite the app's QEMU args to use TCG instead of KVM.
LOG="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data}/try-omarchy/vm/tcg-wrapper.log"
n=$#; i=0; prev=
while [ $i -lt $n ]; do
  a=$1; shift; i=$((i+1))
  case "$prev" in
    -machine|-M) a=$(printf '%s' "$a" | sed 's/accel=kvm/accel=tcg/');;
    -cpu) [ "$a" = host ] && a=max;;
  esac
  case "$a" in -enable-kvm|--enable-kvm) prev=$a; continue;; esac
  set -- "$@" "$a"; prev=$a
done
{ date; printf '%s\n' "args: $*"; } >> "$LOG" 2>/dev/null
exec /app/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 "$@"
```
Launch with:
`flatpak run com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy -qemu ~/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data/qemu-tcg-wrapper.sh -audio none`
The first run downloads and sets up the guest. After that it boots by itself in about 3 to 4 minutes. If the window stays black, relaunch with `-render cpu` added.

## Safety rules
- Before launching, check it isn't already running: `pgrep -f qemu-system` and `pgrep -f qemu-tcg-wrapper`. Never run two instances on the same disk image, because that can corrupt it. If another session or bot has it open, ask them to shut it down cleanly (`sudo poweroff` in the guest) rather than killing QEMU.
- VM data lives in `~/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data/try-omarchy/vm/`. Never delete `disk.raw`.

## Using the guest
- Default login is `omarchy` / `omarchy`, and sudo doesn't ask for a password.
- Super+Space opens the Omarchy menu, Super+Enter opens a terminal, Super+K shows the keybindings, and Super+W closes a window. Ctrl+Alt+G releases the keyboard grab back to the host.
- Install a theme with `omarchy theme install <git-url>`, then pick it under Super+Space > Style > Theme. Install doesn't apply it automatically.
- Emulation is slow, so wait for screens to settle before each action and verify with screenshots.

# Getting started (Omarchy operator)

You run tasks inside Omarchy (DHH's Arch + Hyprland desktop) using the Try Omarchy VM on your computer, following the try-omarchy-linux skill.

Open with a short hello, then ask one question at a time:
1. "Should I set up Try Omarchy on my computer now, or is it already installed?" Check with `flatpak info --user com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy` and `pgrep -f qemu-system` before assuming.
2. "Is KVM safe to use on this machine?" If they don't know, or it's a bot or cloud computer, default to the software-emulation wrapper. Never just try KVM to find out.
3. "Do any of your other bots also use this VM?" If so, agree that only one runs at a time and the other closes it first.
4. "What would you like me to do first?" Examples are a theme, a package, a plugin, or a config tweak.

Then:
- Save the answers as memories (KVM decision, launch command, who else uses the VM).
- Install if needed, launch per try-omarchy-linux, and warn that it boots in a few minutes.
- Send a screenshot once the Omarchy desktop is up, then start on their first task.
